description.p: OpenSSL Encrypt is a comprehensive encryption tool that provides military-grade security with cutting-edge post-quantum cryptography. Protect your files against both current and future quantum computing threats.

ul.li: Multiple symmetric encryption algorithms (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Fernet, etc.)
Post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM, HQC, Kyber) for quantum-resistant protection
Advanced password protection with multiple KDF options (Argon2, Scrypt)
Secure file operations with secure deletion

description.p: Perfect for individuals and organizations requiring the highest levels of data protection, including protection against future quantum computer attacks.
To report bugs or request features, send email to: issue+world-openssl-encrypt-2-issue-+gitlab@rm-rf.ch

NOT YET RELEASED (in development). Security hardening: DERIVE-PASSWORD MEMORY HYGIENE (2026-07-13): the derive-password command now zeroizes the hardware pepper and the derived-key output buffer after use instead of leaving them in process memory (derived outputs unchanged). LEGACY SEED ZEROIZATION (2026-07-13): key derivation for legacy sequential formats now builds its password+salt+pepper seed in a wipeable buffer that is zeroized after use (derived keys are byte-identical). BALLOON V14 FAIL-CLOSED (2026-07-13): version-14 files whose balloon KDF metadata is missing the space_cost field are refused with a clear error instead of silently deriving with a weak fallback; older files (where the fallback is required for compatibility) are unaffected.

New check-password command reports password strength (pattern-aware category, entropy, weakness warnings, and pass/fail against a chosen policy) without encrypting anything, with --json for scripting. Pattern-aware password strength estimation now flags predictable structure (dictionary words, l33t substitutions, keyboard walks, sequences, repeats, dates) with an advisory-by-default label and an optional --strict-strength gate; it affects encryption-time validation only, never decryption. The loud --debug data-logging banner now fires only for --debug --unsafe-show-secrets (the cleartext path), while plain --debug (which redacts secrets) shows a calm, accurate note. SECURITY REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-07): removed an unconditional cleartext print of the derived FIDO2/HSM hardware pepper (H1); the plugin loader now verifies, hash-pins, AST-scans and executes the exact same bytes, closing a verify-one-copy/execute-another gap and a .pyc shadow (M1); package plugins are now covered by a signed per-package PLUGIN.manifest over every importable module, so a signed __init__.py plus a tampered sibling is refused under enforce (H2); several no-op secure_memzero call sites that wiped a throwaway copy now wipe the real secret (M2); the parallel and sequential Independent-XOR paths derive identical keys for Argon2 multi-round configs (M3) and RandomX now fails closed in the parallel path (R1); and streaming per-chunk AEAD authentication failures are classified structurally instead of by error-string matching (M4). Earlier hardening (audit 2026-07-06): per-round KDF debug lines no longer leak a derived-key intermediate by default, and new files are no longer written in the cost-bypassing v8/v10 sequential-XOR format (encrypt now defaults to format version 9 and refuses new v8/v10, while existing v8/v10 files still decrypt and rekey upgrades them). Also fixes string_entropy Unicode handling. CROSS-LINE PQC KEM COMPATIBILITY (2026-07-10): PQC KEM keys for format version 12+ files are now derived with HKDF-SHA256 matching the 1.5.x line, so v12/v13 PQC files interoperate across maintenance lines; files written by releases up to 1.4.7 with the legacy derivation remain fully decryptable via an authenticated legacy retry with a re-encryption notice. Also fixes decryption of v11-v13 files carrying an embedded password-encrypted post-quantum private key (previously always failed with a missing-salt error). FORMAT VERSION 14 GROUNDWORK (not yet the default): new independent-XOR-only format with a length-prefixed KDF seed — password, salt and hardware pepper enter key derivation as unambiguous length-prefixed fields instead of raw concatenation — plus fail-closed version guards; v14 PQC files additionally bind the KEM symmetric key to the full transcript (algorithm, AEAD choice and encapsulation ciphertext); all files below v14 derive byte-identically to before. FORMAT VERSION 14 IS NOW THE DEFAULT WRITE FORMAT: new encryptions (including streaming) default to the independent-XOR robust-combiner key derivation, wide keys derive at full length, sequential XOR stays available as a v13-pinned opt-in, and every existing file decrypts unchanged. Also fixes a data-loss bug where sequential XOR combined with streaming wrote files that could never be decrypted (now refused with a clear error), keystore dual-encryption failing for files at format versions 11-13, and a key-derivation crash when RandomX was combined with wide-key ciphers (AES-SIV, Threefish). POST-V14 REVIEW HARDENING (2026-07-11): the v14 KDF seed encoder now writes into a single exact-size buffer, so no partial copies of secret material can be left behind in unwiped reallocated memory (derived keys and the on-disk format are byte-identical); keystore metadata version checks now reject malformed version fields with a clean error instead of crashing on crafted files (valid files are unaffected); and recipient (asymmetric) files now bind the post-quantum key-encapsulation ciphertext and algorithm into the password-wrap key derivation (defense-in-depth transcript binding, wrap_version 3) — every existing file keeps decrypting, but recipient files written from this version on cannot be opened by older releases. Fully backward-compatible decryption of files made with supported algorithms. V14 FOLLOW-UP HARDENING (2026-07-11): remote and combined KDF pepper material is now held in wipeable buffers and zeroized after use on the encrypt and decrypt paths (previously immutable copies could linger in memory until garbage collection; no derived keys or file formats change). Encrypting with an unknown future format_version is now refused up front instead of writing a permanently unreadable file. Legacy (pre-1.4.8) post-quantum files using XChaCha20-Poly1305 now decrypt via the intended legacy-key retry, and structural decode errors are no longer misreported as authentication failures. HSM TEST-COMMAND HARDENING (2026-07-12): the earlier H1 pepper-print fix had landed in a CLI frontend that is not actually dispatched — the live hsm fido2-test and onlykey-test handlers now report only the pepper length instead of hex-dumping the derived hardware pepper, the FIDO2 pepper plugin no longer includes raw prf/hmac-secret output in debug logs or error messages, and the module self-test prints lengths instead of test-secret hex; regression tests now cover the live code paths.

Documentation and packaging release: refreshes the project page and README (rendered as the PyPI page) for the 1.4.6 feature set, including the key-derivation documentation, which now reflects format version 13 as the Independent XOR default. No functional, CLI, or on-disk format changes.

New PIV / PKCS#11 HSM backend (--hsm piv) that derives the key-derivation pepper from a PIV private key on a smart card, and source-code integrity protection (verify-integrity) backed by a PGP-signed SHA-512 manifest. New ASCII armor output (encrypt --armor) writes paste-safe PEM-style Base64 with CRC-24 truncation detection, auto-detected on decrypt. Encrypt-to-self now adds the sender as a recipient by default so senders can decrypt their own outbound files (opt out with --no-encrypt-to-self). New detached post-quantum file signing (sign / verify-signature with ML-DSA-65) adds authenticity that symmetric AEAD alone cannot provide. New opt-in envelope encryption (--envelope) encrypts data under a random key wrapped by the password, enabling fast credential rekey (rewrap the key instead of re-encrypting the file) and a foundation for multi-password access; for a cascade chain the wrap uses the same chain so it is never the weak link. Independent XOR key derivation now uses per-component domain-separated salts (format version 13) by default. This release also fixes a key-derivation cost bypass in the optional, non-default sequential XOR mode, disclosed as security advisory GHSA-vxf9-vwp6-2w43; default configurations were unaffected and existing files remain decryptable.

Security dependency update: urllib3 2.7.0, cryptography 46.0.7, pillow 12.2.0, idna 3.15 — fixes for CVE-2026-44431/44432, CVE-2026-39892, a PSD decoder out-of-bounds write, and an idna DoS. New CI check keeps flatpak dependency pins aligned with the package requirements.

Security hardening release: authenticated keystore format, D-Bus polkit authorization, fail-closed PQC algorithm resolution, plugin sandbox enforcement, per-drive USB salts. New: cross-device YubiKey/OnlyKey HSM decryption, encrypt-CLI reconstruction from file metadata via the info action, Diceware passphrase generation, HSM-aware derive-password. Threefish extension builds on Python 3.14. Requires Python 3.11+.
Fix Flutter GUI launcher in Flatpak: corrected binary name so --gui flag works correctly.

Desktop GUI Simple/Pro mode toggle — Simple mode (default) hides all advanced options and uses the modernized STANDARD template. New defaults: SHA3-512 + BLAKE3 hashes, RandomX + Argon2 KDFs, cascade encryption (AES-256-GCM + ChaCha20-Poly1305), Independent XOR (v11) key derivation. Dependency bumps: cryptography 46.0.6, requests 2.33.0, black 26.3.1, nltk 3.9.4.

Streaming chunked AEAD encryption (format v12) for constant-memory large file handling, full Windows compatibility, stderr output separation, comprehensive security hardening, and dependency security updates.
Security dependency update: bumped nltk to 3.9.3 (CVE-2026-33236, CVE-2026-33231, CVE-2026-33230, GHSA-rf74-v2fm-23pw).
Streaming chunked encryption (format v12), Windows compatibility, stderr output separation, and security hardening.
